scenes.title: Turkey
scenes.subtitle: A history told only by its sources

scenes.caption: Photo 1920
scenes.text: From the time when parts of what is now Turkey were conquered by the Seljuq dynasty, the history of Turkey spans the medieval history of the Seljuk Empire, the medieval to modern history of the Ottoman Empire, and the history of…

scenes.caption: Photo 1873 · Istanbul
scenes.text: The Urfa Man statue is dated c. 9000 BC, to the period of the Pre-Pottery Neolithic, and is defined as "the oldest known naturalistic life-sized sculpture of a human".

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Istanbul
scenes.text: Troy's earliest layers go back to around 4500 BC.

scenes.caption: Photo 1873 · Istanbul
scenes.text: Anatolia's historical records start with clay tablets from approximately around 2000 BC that were found in modern-day Kültepe.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Istanbul
scenes.text: The Persian Achaemenid Empire fell to Alexander the Great in 334 BC, which led to increasing cultural homogeneity and Hellenization in the area.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Istanbul
scenes.text: Following Alexander's death in 323 BC, Anatolia was subsequently divided into a number of small Hellenistic kingdoms, all of which became part of the Roman Republic by the mid-1st century BC.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Istanbul
scenes.text: Following the death of Theodosius I in 395 and the permanent division of the Roman Empire between his two sons, the city, which would popularly come to be known as Constantinople became the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Istanbul
scenes.text: Historically they were established after the 6th century BC.

scenes.caption: Photo 1873 · Istanbul
scenes.text: The earliest separate Turkic peoples appeared on the peripheries of the late Xiongnu confederation about 200 BC (contemporaneous with the Chinese Han Dynasty).

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Istanbul
scenes.text: The Hun hordes of Attila, who invaded and conquered much of Europe in the 5th century AD, may have been Turkic and descendants of the Xiongnu.

scenes.caption: Photo 1873 · Istanbul
scenes.text: The Seljuq/Seljuk empire was founded by Tughril Beg (1016–1063) in 1037.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: The Ottoman beylik's first capital was located in Bursa in 1326.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: Edirne which was conquered in 1361 was the next capital city.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: After largely expanding to Europe and Anatolia, in 1453, the Ottomans nearly completed the conquest of the Byzantine Empire by capturing its capital, Constantinople during the reign of Mehmed II.

scenes.caption: Photo 1941
scenes.text: The Treaty of Lausanne of 24 July 1923, which superseded the Treaty of Sèvres, led to the international recognition of the sovereignty of the new Turkish state as the successor state of the Ottoman Empire.

scenes.caption: Photo 1941
scenes.text: Atatürk's reforms caused discontent in some Kurdish and Zaza tribes leading to the Sheikh Said rebellion in 1925 and the Dersim rebellion in 1937.

scenes.caption: Photo 1941
scenes.text: In April 2017, the constitutional amendments, which significantly increased the powers of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, were narrowly accepted in the constitutional referendum.

scenes.title: What the sources leave out
scenes.text: Between 1016 and 1326, the sources consulted give no precise date.
